description.narrative:
Voices from the Camps: Youth-Led Evidence <(>&<)> Advocacy for Education and Health Rights in North-East Nigeria is a youth-driven initiative giving hope and voice to young people whose lives have been shaped by Boko Haram violence, displacement, floods, and the loss of schools and health services. In IDP camps and host communities across Borno and Yobe States, youth aged 18–35 will be trained as researchers and advocates to turn their lived pain into evidence and action. They will document barriers to education and healthcare, lead community dialogues, and stand before leaders to demand change. Through powerful storytelling, media and policy engagement, their voices will travel beyond the camps. At a time when humanitarian support is shrinking, this project will raise a new generation of confident youth leaders who can stand on their own and shape a future where every young person is heard and every right matters.
The goal is to empower displaced youth in Banki, Bama, Dikwa and Ngala in Borno State, and inDamaturu and Gujba in Yobe State, to influence education and health decisions affecting their lives. In these IDP camps and host communities, young people face disrupted schooling, weak health services, and exclusion from local planning. The project willtrain youth as researchers and advocates, collect evidence, hold community dialogues, and lead advocacy forums. Lessons and youth demands from these sites will inform wider engagement with authorities, contributing to youth-responsive education and health actions across North-East Nigeria.

participating-org.narrative:
Kambiya Development Initiative (KDI) is a youth-led, community-based organisation working to improve the wellbeing and resilience of vulnerable and marginalised communities in North-East Nigeria, particularly those affected by conflict, displacement, poverty, andlimited access to basic services.
Our vision is to become one of the most impactful humanitarian and development organisations in North-East Nigeria by 2040, transforming lives through empathy, equity, and empowerment.
Our mission is to address the pressing challenges faced by vulnerable communities by driving sustainable development in the areas of poverty alleviation, zero hunger, healthcare, education, clean water, economic empowerment, climate action, peacebuilding, and partnerships, in alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals.
Our objectives include:
improving access to quality education and essential health services for marginalised children and youth; strengthening community resilience through youth-led initiatives and local solutions; amplifying the voices of underrepresented young people in decision-making and policy processes; and building partnerships with government, civil society, and humanitarian actors to deliver sustainable impact. Our values are grounded in empathy for vulnerable people, equity and inclusion ofmarginalised groups, youth leadership and participation, accountability and transparency, community ownership, and collaboration for impact.
Through youth-driven action, evidence-based advocacy, and strong community engagement, KDI is committed to enabling youngpeople to become agents of change and to contributing to peace, development, and social justice in North-East Nigeria.
